chunks: And from Ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from one of the scholars, that he said:

When a believer dies, his two angels ascend (to the heavens) and say, 'O Lord, so-and-so has passed away.' So He (Allah) says (to them), 'Descend and pray beside his grave, glorifying and magnifying Me until the Day of Resurrection, and record what you do for him.'
ai.seo_question: What do the angels do at the grave of a believer after death?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Mumin* highlights the unique intercessory role of angels for the faithful, emphasizing that their continuous glorification (*tahlil* and *takbir*) at the grave serves as a perpetual record of merit until the Day of Resurrection. In Shia scholarly tradition, this underscores the concept of *barakah* extending beyond death, where the spiritual status of the believer is actively maintained by divine agents, reinforcing the importance of righteous deeds in life as they are 'written' and preserved in the celestial record.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 70. It has been reported that Abu al-Bilad from his father, from one of the scholars that he said:

When a believer dies, his two angels ascend (to the heavens) and say, 'O Lord, so-and-so has passed away.' So He (Allah) says (to them), 'Descend and pray besides his grave, magnifying and glorifying Me until the Day of Resurrection, and record your actions for him (as his reward).'
